measures.name: Remove the two-child limit in Universal Credit from April 2026

parameters.label: Children the Universal Credit child element is paid for
Children Child Tax Credit is paid for (legacy claims)
parameters.note: Tax credits ended in April 2025; set as PolicyEngine's own analysis sets it, for any claim the survey still records.

measures.name: Keep the 5p cut in fuel duty to August 2026, then bring it back in three steps

parameters.label: Main rate of fuel duty, £ a litre, averaged over the year

pre_source.note: Without the Budget the cut would have ended on 22 March 2026 (57.95p a litre), with RPI rises after. Both paths are PolicyEngine's: its pre-Budget rates, rounded to the penny, and its current law, which averages each calendar year (52.95p to August 2026, then 53.95p, 55.95p and 57.95p).

measures.name: Keep income tax and National Insurance thresholds frozen for three more years, to April 2031

parameters.label: Personal allowance, £ a year

pre_source.where: Section 57: CPI indexation, increases rounded up to a multiple of £10
pre_source.note: CPI from PolicyEngine UK 2.102.3's OBR index (gov.economic_assumptions.indices.obr.consumer_price_index), 2.0% a year.

parameters.label: Basic rate band (taxable income at which the higher rate starts), £ a year

pre_source.where: Section 57: CPI indexation, increases rounded up to a multiple of £100
pre_source.note: CPI from PolicyEngine UK 2.102.3's OBR index, 2.0% a year.

parameters.label: National Insurance primary threshold, £ a week (the personal allowance ÷ 52)

pre_source.note: The primary threshold follows the personal allowance (£12,570 a year is 241.73 a week).

parameters.label: National Insurance upper earnings limit, £ a week (the higher rate threshold ÷ 52)

pre_source.note: The upper earnings limit follows the higher rate threshold, the allowance plus the basic rate band (£50,270 a year is 966.73 a week).

parameters.label: Self-employed lower profits limit, £ a year (the personal allowance)

pre_source.note: The lower profits limit follows the personal allowance. PolicyEngine UK 2.102.3 uprates it from 2027-28, a year early; both values are set here.

parameters.label: Self-employed upper profits limit, £ a year (the higher rate threshold)

pre_source.note: The upper profits limit follows the higher rate threshold.

measures.note: Without the Budget the freeze would have ended in April 2028. The allowance and the basic rate band would then have risen with September's CPI, rounded up to the next £10 and £100 as the law requires, using the OBR's forecast of 2% a year; the National Insurance thresholds stay aligned with them.

measures.name: Keep employers' National Insurance threshold at £5,000 to April 2031

parameters.label: Employers' secondary threshold, £ a week

pre_source.note: Without the Budget the threshold (£5,000 a year, 96 a week) would have risen with CPI from April 2028, 2% a year in the OBR's forecast.

measures.note: PolicyEngine counts employers' National Insurance as paid by their employees, through lower pay (gov.contrib.policyengine.employer_ni.employee_incidence is 1), so this measure lowers household incomes; the Treasury counts it as a tax on business.

measures.note: PolicyEngine estimates which households own such homes from survey data on property values; the surcharge rises with CPI from April 2029.

measures.name: Freeze rail fares in England for a year from March 2026

not_modelled.note: PolicyEngine has no rail fare rules a policy can change; its own analysis adds the Treasury's cost (£145 million in 2026-27) to households in proportion to their spending on rail, in extra code.

measures.name: Freeze the Plan 2 student loan repayment threshold for three years from April 2027

not_modelled.note: PolicyEngine's public model takes student loan repayments as the survey records them, so a new threshold changes nothing without extra code (its own analysis adds it). The Treasury scores about £0.3 billion a year from 2027-28, paid by graduates earning above the threshold.

measures.name: Keep inheritance tax thresholds frozen for a further year, to April 2031

not_modelled.note: PolicyEngine UK does not model inheritance tax, which falls on estates rather than on a household's yearly income.

measures.name: A mileage charge on electric and plug-in hybrid cars from April 2028

not_modelled.note: A new tax, so the model has no rules for it. The Treasury expects it to raise £1.1 billion in 2028-29.

treasury.title: Impact of decisions from Autumn Budget 2024 onwards on households in 2028-29, as a percentage of net income, by income decile
treasury.covers: every tax, welfare and public spending decision since Autumn Budget 2024, not only this Budget's, in 2028-29, including the value of public services households use
treasury.differs: The Treasury's chart is for 2028-29, counts every decision since Autumn Budget 2024 rather than this Budget's alone, and adds the value of public services; ours counts only this Budget's tax and benefit measures that PolicyEngine can model, in cash, for each year.

compared_with.name: PolicyEngine's own analysis of Autumn Budget 2025
compared_with.note: PolicyEngine published its own decile results on 9 December 2025, from an earlier version of its model. docs/MODEL.md (T1, "Rehearsal") compares the two and explains each gap.

input.note: Two measures announced before the Budget and only scored in its table are left out, as they were not decisions of this Budget: Winter Fuel Payment for pensioners with taxable income up to £35,000 (line 84) and the Universal Credit standard allowance and health element changes (line 85).
